Before that recovery the largest all-matching run was 14 functions (ordinals 41..54); after the four literal-pool folds it was 26 (ordinals 14..39); with ordinal 40 it is 41. The FOUR contiguous all-matching runs as merged are 0..12 (13), 14..54 (41), 56..59 (4) and 61..79 (19); this is the largest.

FIVE of the seven never-matched shards were recovered while merging, and they are inside the licensed run: func_ov006_020d5fd8, _020d6264 and _020d65b4 each fold `+0x6200` and their field offset into one literal-pool constant, where the cartridge keeps `add rN,rN,#0x6200` and a separate `strh [rN,#off]`; a struct with the field at that offset restores the split. func_ov006_020d672c is the same defect twice over (0x6000 and 0x6200 bases). func_ov006_020d6784's only defect was field-address CSE across a read-modify-write of the score at +0xbc: the cartridge re-issues `ldr r0,#0xbc` / `str`, mwcc hoists `add r3,r0,#0xbc`; writing the store through `volatile unsigned int *` defeats the hoist. All five carried delink blocks WITHOUT the `complete` marker, i.e. dsd was serving the cartridge's bytes for them; folded here they are source-built and byte-verified for the first time.

The destructor pair (ROM ordinals 0 and 1, _ZN14dScMgBomroom_cD1Ev at 0x020d5a54 BELOW D0Ev at 0x020d5a78) is on the far side of the ordinal-13 hole and is NOT in this range. dScMgBomroom_c declares its destructor first and out of line, so the destructor is the class's key function; with the key function outside the licensed range this TU emits no _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS and compiler_only_output is empty -- the 2*(ancestors+self)+1 row-count formula does not apply. include/dScMgBomroom_c.h is NOT edited by this promotion.

notes: Assembled by hand from tools/tubuild.py's parsed shard data: `tubuild.py create ov006/dScMgBomroom_c` ABORTS on this TU with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'relative_to' (tubuild.py:959). build_manifest_entry calls SP.path_for(name).relative_to(REPO) unconditionally, which contradicts cmd_create's own comment at tubuild.py:987-995 that a sourceless member 'becomes a banner'. assemble_shadow_source handles it; the manifest builder does not. The .cpp is written before the crash, so the shadow source exists with no manifest entry.
Written ROM-ASCENDING because `#pragma defer_codegen off` makes CodeWarrior emit each definition as it is encountered rather than in reverse source order.

include/decl_common.h declares seven of this TU's members. Six are `void f(void*)`; their definitions here take that spelling and cast to the recovered type on the first line, which is byte-neutral (41/41 with the casts in place). The seventh, func_ov006_020d672c, was declared `int f()` -- decl_headers.py had read the legacy shard's K&R forward declaration rather than its definition. The cartridge takes the scene pointer in r0 and leaves r0 untouched on the early-out path, so the header is corrected to `void f(void*)` in the same change; the only other caller, src/_ZN14dScMgBomroom_c6RenderEv.cpp, declares it locally and does not include decl_common.h.

Each member keeps its own legacy shadow types, suffixed with the member's address (S_604c, Obj_6098, PMF_6278, ...) so that fourteen shards' independently-invented `S`/`C`/`Rec`/`Obj`/`Work`/`Ent`/`Entry` tags coexist. Members derived from .c shards had their `this` parameter renamed to `self_` -- a C++ keyword in the merged TU.
